name: Settings
purpose: The app’s Settings tab and every screen it opens in the app today: Face ID, Your app data, and signing out, through the confirmation, to You’ve signed out. Their pages link to each other as the app’s screens do.
when: Prototyping a new setting, or a change to an existing one.
Prototyping a new screen opened from Settings, such as a page about the user’s account or data.
Prototyping a journey that starts in Settings, such as signing out or managing notifications.
Testing a change to the wording of Settings or the screens it opens.
screen: Settings, the root of the Settings tab, and the screens it opens: Face ID, Your app data, the sign-out confirmation and You’ve signed out

screens.title: Settings
screens.description: The root of the Settings tab, with the app’s own rows. Face ID, Your app data and Sign out open the other screens.

screens.title: Face ID
screens.description: Opened from the Face ID row. Explains Face ID, with a button to change it in the phone’s settings, and a back button to Settings.

screens.title: Your app data
screens.description: Opened from the Your app data row. Explains the data the app keeps, with a button to request it, and a back button to Settings.

screens.title: Are you sure you want to sign out?
screens.description: Opened from the Sign out row, as a sheet over Settings. Sign out goes on to You’ve signed out; Cancel and close return to Settings.

screens.title: You’ve signed out
screens.description: After signing out. Signing in again returns to Settings.

ios.symbol: SignOutConfirmationCoordinator, which presents it as a sheet

notes: Copy the whole folder, so the screens keep linking to each other. Delete the screens you don’t need, and the rows that open them.
Each page has a comment at its top saying what to change and what to leave.
Your accounts, Messages, Notifications and Open source licences go nowhere, as the library has no screens for them. Give a row an href to a page of yours to make it open one.
Home on the tab bar opens the Home template, if it’s beside this one. Chat goes nowhere.
Signing out and signing in again only move between pages: nothing is remembered.
